verses.text: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo spoke to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak got up and started building God’s house in Jerusalem. God’s prophets were right there helping them.
Around that time Tattenai, governor beyond the River, came with Shetharbozenai and their companions. They asked, “Who gave you the order to build this house and finish this wall?”
They also asked for the names of the men putting up the building.
But their God was watching over the Jewish elders. The officials didn’t make them stop while the matter went to Darius and they waited for his written reply.
Here’s a copy of the letter to King Darius from Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shetharbozenai, and his companions, the Apharsachites who lived beyond the River.
The letter they sent him said, “To King Darius, wishing you every peace.

The king should know that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. They’re building it with large stones and setting timbers into the walls. They’re working hard, and the job is going well.
We asked the elders, ‘Who gave you the order to build this house and finish this wall?’
We also asked their names so we could write down who was leading them and let you know.
Here’s the answer they gave us: ‘We’re servants of the God of heaven and earth. We’re rebuilding the house that stood here many years ago, the one a great king of Israel built and finished.
But our ancestors provoked the God of heaven to anger. He handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean, king of Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed this house and took the people away to Babylon.
Then in the first year of Cyrus as king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued an order to rebuild this house of God.

Nebuchadnezzar had taken the gold and silver vessels from God’s house, moving them from the temple in Jerusalem to the temple in Babylon. King Cyrus took them back out of the temple in Babylon and had them handed over to Sheshbazzar, whom he’d appointed governor.
He told him, “Take these vessels and put them in the temple in Jerusalem. Have God’s house built on its own site.”
That same Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God’s house in Jerusalem. Work has gone on since then, but the house still isn’t finished.’

So now, if it pleases the king, please have someone search the royal treasury in Babylon to see whether King Cyrus actually issued an order to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem. Please send us your decision on the matter.”
